title: Clean/dirty workflow, transport and traceability
audience: Cleaners and cleaning supervisors who move equipment, trolleys and supplies around a healthcare facility, in any Australian state or territory. This course covers external cleaning only.
referencesAtStart: Official sources for this lesson: NHMRC, Australian Guidelines for the Prevention and Control of Infection in Healthcare (2019) (no page date shown; document dated 2019); NDIS Practice Standards and Quality Indicators, Version 4, Core Module (cover date November 2021; no page date shown).
learningOutcomes: Plan a clean-to-dirty route for a trolley and its contents before work begins.
Keep used equipment, used cloths and contaminated materials separate from clean stock during transport.
Complete a handoff record so that each item can be traced from collection to return.
Identify a route, storage or handoff breach and state the correction and the escalation.

instruction.heading: Scope of this lesson: external cleaning only
instruction.body: This lesson covers external cleaning only. It explains how a cleaner plans and records the movement of equipment and materials around a healthcare site. Reprocessing, disinfection for reusable devices and sterilisation are outside this course. They are authorised only by the manufacturer's instructions and the facility's written procedure, and the movement of an item for those purposes follows the facility procedure rather than this lesson.

instruction.heading: Why the direction of travel matters
instruction.body: Healthcare facilities usually separate clean areas from used or contaminated areas so that clean stock does not pick up contamination on the way past. The NHMRC Australian Guidelines for the Prevention and Control of Infection in Healthcare treat environmental controls, including cleaning and spill management, as part of preventing transmission from the environment to patients. The practical rule is one-way movement: clean stock moves from clean areas to point of use, and used items move from point of use to a designated holding area, without crossing back through clean areas. The shortest route is not always the correct route. If the shortest path crosses a soiled holding corridor, the facility's designated route applies, even when it takes longer.

instruction.heading: Planning the trolley and its contents
instruction.body: Before you leave the clean store, check the trolley's content list against the work order. Keep clean cloths, containers, product and equipment in their own compartments, and keep used cloths in a bag or bin that is closed and labelled. Never load used equipment onto a trolley that carries clean stock, and do not use one trolley for both unless the facility procedure says so. Confirm the route, the lift or door you will use, and the holding area for used items. Plan the order of the round so that you move from the cleanest area to the most soiled, as the facility procedure directs.

instruction.heading: Transport, containment and handoff
instruction.body: Transport items so that they are covered, secured and cannot fall or leak. An item that must be moved to a designated area is placed in a labelled container where the procedure requires one, and you do not carry several items in your hands at once. At each handoff, the receiving person confirms the item, the condition and the destination, and you record the handoff. A handoff is not complete until the receiving person accepts it. If the receiving person is not available, keep the item in the designated holding area and do not leave it on a corridor floor or in a clean area.

instruction.heading: Traceability
instruction.body: Traceability means that you can say, for any item, where it came from, where it went, who handled it and when. A simple record with the item identity, the time, the location and the handoff signature is usually enough, but the exact record format is set by the facility. Traceability lets the team act if an item is later found to be damaged, unlabelled, or in the wrong place. A cleaner who moves an item without recording it breaks the chain and makes it impossible to tell whether the item was cleaned, moved or left in an unsafe place.

procedure: Check the work order and the trolley content list before leaving the clean store.
Confirm the designated route, the holding area for used items, and any restricted zones on the site.
Keep clean stock and used items in separate compartments or containers, and do not mix them on the trolley.
Move in the direction the facility procedure specifies, and do not cross back through clean areas with used items.
At each handoff, confirm the item identity, condition and destination with the receiving person.
Record each handoff with the item, time, location and receiving person, and keep the record with the job file.
If a breach occurs, such as a used cloth on clean stock or a route through a clean area, stop, separate the affected items, and tell the supervisor.

workedExamples.situation: Your clean trolley must reach a treatment room. The shortest route passes a soiled holding corridor where used cloths are waiting to be collected.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: Which route do you take, and what do you record?
workedExamples.reasoning: Use the facility's designated route, even if it is longer, so the clean trolley does not pass the soiled holding area. Record the route used and the time. If the designated route is blocked, tell the supervisor before moving, rather than taking the shorter route on your own.

workedExamples.situation: At a handoff, the receiving person asks you to leave a bag of used cloths with a stack of clean cloths on the same shelf, to save a trip.
workedExamples.reasoning: Decline. Used cloths must not share a shelf with clean stock. Take the used bag to the designated holding area, keep the clean stock separate, and record the handoff. Explain the reason briefly so the receiving person understands the rule.

commonErrors.error: Taking the shortest route through a soiled area to save time.
commonErrors.prevention: Use the designated route. If it is blocked, tell the supervisor before moving.

commonErrors.error: Loading used cloths or items next to clean stock on the same trolley shelf.
commonErrors.prevention: Keep used and clean items in separate compartments or containers at all times.

commonErrors.error: Leaving a handoff open because the receiving person is busy.
commonErrors.prevention: Hold the item in the designated holding area until the handoff is accepted and recorded.

commonErrors.error: Moving an item without a record, so its route cannot be traced.
commonErrors.prevention: Record every handoff with the item, time, location and receiving person.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: This course covers external cleaning only. Reprocessing, disinfection for reusable devices and sterilisation are outside the course and are authorised only by the manufacturer's instructions and the facility procedure.

The NHMRC Australian Guidelines for the Prevention and Control of Infection in Healthcare (2019) treat environmental controls, including cleaning and spill management, as part of preventing transmission from the environment to patients (section 2.2; document dated 2019).

The NDIS Practice Standards, Version 4 of November 2021, Core Module, require that the management of infectious waste includes policies for storing, handling and disposing of it, including used PPE, and that workers who handle waste are trained. Where the facility is an NDIS provider, these requirements apply to the facility.
Licence notice: Moving or transporting regulated medical or clinical waste may require a state or territory permit or licence. This lesson does not grant any transport authority.

qualityStandard: The learner plans a route on a supplied site map that avoids crossing a soiled area with clean stock.
The learner sorts a supplied trolley content list into clean and used compartments with no mixing.
The learner completes a handoff record for three supplied items with item, time, location and receiving person.
The learner identifies the breach in a supplied scenario and gives the correction and escalation step.
documentationEvidence: Route taken and any deviation, with the reason and the supervisor notified
Handoff record for each item: identity, time, location, receiving person and acceptance
Any breach, its correction, and the escalation recipient
summary: Clean and used items move in one direction and are kept separate on the trolley.
The designated route applies even if the shortest route is faster.
A handoff is complete only when the receiving person accepts it and it is recorded.
Traceability depends on a record for every item, every time.

knowledgeChecks.question: The shortest route with a clean trolley passes a soiled holding corridor. What should the cleaner do?
options: Take the shortest route, since the trolley is covered.
Use the designated route, and tell the supervisor if it is blocked.
Pass through quickly without stopping, so the corridor is not contaminated.

knowledgeChecks.question: Which arrangement is correct on a trolley?
options: Used cloths on the same shelf as clean cloths to save space.
Used items in the clean compartment, labelled for later collection.
Used and clean items in separate compartments or containers.

knowledgeChecks.question: When is a handoff complete?
options: When the receiving person accepts the item and the handoff is recorded.
When the item is placed on the nearest shelf, where the next person can find it
When the cleaner leaves the area, since the job is then finished for the day
